title: Kestrel and the Hollow
premise: Paloma Sterling, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Kestrel, has spent ten years selling harmless charms in Vharrow, a city where magic is outlawed. When a dying courier presses a map of the court beneath Mount Hollow into his hands, Paloma learns his own name is written in its margins — sold to the Undercourt a decade ago, along with his memories of the god he serves. Guided by a found family of outcasts — a disgraced archivist, a child who remembers everything she reads, and a thief with no shadow — he descends to steal back his soul before the Hollow's magistrates finish consuming it. In the end, Paloma chooses to shatter his own soul rather than let the court keep it, freeing the god Kestrel's scattered voice and discovering that family, not divinity, was the power worth keeping.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped sea caves off the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about broken oaths, borrowed names, and the people who choose each other anyway.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In outlawed Vharrow, Paloma sells trinkets that almost work, hiding his hollow oath-mark beneath his sleeve. A routine protection job for a spice merchant goes wrong when his charm actually ignites, drawing the attention of the Wardens. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a man serving a god who no longer answers, and the fear of being seen.

chapters.title: The Dying Courier
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A stranger collapses in Paloma's doorway, blood on his lips and a wax-sealed map in his fist. With his last breath he says Paloma's true name — a name Paloma doesn't remember owning — and warns him: 'The Hollow keeps what it buys.' Wardens pound on the door. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo as the ground of Paloma's identity cracks open.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Burned Her Library
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleeing the Wardens, Paloma seeks Odile Vane, a disgraced archivist exiled for reading forbidden texts. She deciphers the map: the Undercourt beneath Mount Hollow, where souls are sold as currency. The margins list Paloma's name, dated ten years ago — the night Kestrel went silent. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; the first hint that his silence was theft, not abandonment.

chapters.title: A Girl Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recruits Wren, an eleven-year-old orphan whose perfect memory makes her a living record of everything the Wardens burned. Wren has memorized a fragment of the Hollow's purchase ledger — including a line about 'the Kestrel-bearer, soul intact, reserved.' Emotional beat: Odile, who lost her own family to the court, recognizing the found family assembling itself around Paloma's quest.

chapters.title: The Thief Without a Shadow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The last companion is Sef, a thief who sold his shadow to the Undercourt for passage out of debt and now casts nothing. Sef knows the mountain's servant tunnels but warns the price of entry: every traveler must surrender one memory at the gate. Paloma realizes he has almost nothing left to surrender. Emotional beat: dark humor and kinship among the damaged; the party becomes a family in name.

chapters.title: The Gate of Small Surrenders
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The party descends through the servant tunnels. At the gate, each pays a memory: Odile gives her wedding day, Sef gives his mother's face, Wren gives her first snowfall. Paloma offers a memory and the gate rejects it — he has none to give; his were taken in advance. Emotional beat: grief for what's surrendered, and the horror of Paloma's pre-emptive hollowing.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Undercourt revealed: magistrates in bone masks who trade souls like coin, and a vault where Kestrel's stolen voice is kept as collateral. Paloma confronts the magistrate who bought him ten years ago — and learns it was his own oath that was the purchase price; the god was silenced as part of the contract. Emotional beat: rage and betrayal; power's corruption made intimate.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. While Sef and Wren infiltrate the vault, Odile bargains with the court's record-keeper using Wren's memorized ledger fragment — proof of a fraudulent entry that could unravel the magistrates' authority. The magistrates offer Paloma his soul back if he renounces Kestrel and serves them. Emotional beat: temptation; the seductive logic of corrupted power offering comfort at a moral price.

chapters.title: The Shattering
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax. Paloma refuses the bargain and seizes his soul from the vault — but the magistrates move to consume Kestrel's voice to keep him bound. Rather than let either be owned, Paloma shatters his own soul-jar, releasing his memories and the god's voice in a single burst. The Hollow's foundations crack as ten years of stolen memory flood back to every soul the court ever bought. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into liberation.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Hollow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma wakes on the mountainside with fragmented memories and no oath-mark — unbound, unowned. Kestrel speaks at last, not as a master but as an equal, offering friendship instead of service. The found family climbs into the dawn: Odile with her archive of the court's crimes, Wren carrying the truth, Sef's shadow slowly regrowing. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; family and freedom over power and divinity.
